title: Transferred Kan model structure on algebras over a many-sorted theory
statement: Fix a universe and a small set $S$. An $S$-sorted algebraic theory $T$ is a small category with specified finite products and distinguished objects $T_s$ for $s\in S$, such that every object is a finite product of these objects, including the empty product. A strict simplicial $T$-algebra is a finite-product-preserving functor $T\to\mathrm{sSet}$, and a map is a natural transformation. Use simplicial sets, boundaries, horns, weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For every $s$, evaluation $U_s(A)=A(T_s)$ has a left adjoint $F_s$, characterized by $\operatorname{Hom}(F_sK,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,U_sA)$ naturally in $K,A$. The category of strict simplicial $T$-algebras admits a cofibrantly generated model structure with weak equivalences and fibrations detected by every $U_s$. Its generating cofibrations are $F_s(\partial\Delta^n)\to F_s(\Delta^n)$ for $s\in S$, $n\geq0$, and its generating trivial cofibrations are $F_s(\Lambda_i^n)\to F_s(\Delta^n)$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. The two generating families admit functorial small-object factorizations, and cofibrations are exactly retracts of relative generating-cofibration cell maps. Here a relative cell map is a transfinite composite, continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of coproducts of generating maps. A model structure means a complete and cocomplete category with retract-closed weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, and weak factorization systems (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations); trivial means also a weak equivalence, and the factorizations can be chosen functorially. In a weak factorization system each map factors as a left-class map followed by a right-class map, and each class consists exactly of maps with the corresponding lifting property against the other class.

source.place: J. E. Bergner, Rigidification of algebras over multi-sorted theories, Definitions 3.1 and 3.6, evaluation/free adjunction preceding Theorem 4.7, Theorem 4.7 and its proof, printed pp. 1942–1944. Example 3.5 identifies fixed-object categories as an (O times O)-sorted theory. Read online; not archived. No Stacks tag states this transferred enriched model result.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of product-preserving functors $T\to\mathrm{Set}$ and natural transformations. Regard the specified finite-product cones of $T$, including the terminal cone, as a finite-limit sketch. By [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models], $\mathcal C$ has small Hom sets and all small limits and colimits, and its limits and filtered colimits are computed pointwise. Currying identifies strict simplicial $T$-algebras with functors $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$: product preservation is exactly product preservation in each simplicial degree. Form limits and colimits degreewise in $\mathcal C$; the structure maps are induced by their universal properties. This gives completeness and cocompleteness of strict simplicial algebras, with limits and filtered colimits computed at each sort and simplicial degree.

source.place: Theorem 4.7 proof, first paragraph; explicit specialization of the finite-limit-sketch input to finite-product models and then simplicial objects.

proof.text: For $s\in S$, the covariant representable $h_s=T(T_s,-)$ is an object of $\mathcal C$: the product comparison is the bijection $T(T_s,\prod_j t_j)=\prod_jT(T_s,t_j)$, also for the empty product. A natural transformation $h_s\to M$ is determined by the image $m\in M(T_s)$ of $1_{T_s}$, and its component sends $u:T_s\to t$ to $M(u)(m)$; this gives the inverse bijection. For a simplicial set $K$, define $(F_sK)_n=\coprod_{x\in K_n}^{\mathcal C}h_s$, where the coproduct exists by [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models]. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, send the summand indexed by $x$ to that indexed by $K(\alpha)x$ by the identity of $h_s$; these maps satisfy the simplicial identities. The coproduct universal property and the preceding explicit bijection identify a map $F_sK\to A$ with elements of $A(T_s)_n$ indexed by $K_n$, compatible with every $\alpha$, that is a simplicial map $K\to U_sA$. The formulas commute with maps in $K$ and $A$, proving the natural adjunction.

source.place: Evaluation/free adjunction immediately preceding Theorem 4.7, p.1942; explicit copower-of-representables construction of the same left adjoint.

proof.text: Let $I$ and $J$ be the free boundary and horn families in the statement, and let $W$ and $\mathrm{Fib}$ be the sortwise weak equivalences and Kan fibrations. Under the adjunction of step 2, the four maps of a lifting square and its diagonal correspond bijectively to those of its evaluated simplicial-set square, with the two triangle identities preserved. Thus [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] identifies $I^{\pitchfork}=\mathrm{Fib}\cap W$ and $J^{\pitchfork}=\mathrm{Fib}$. In particular the boundary with $n=0$ is included, whereas horns begin with $n=1$. Sortwise two-out-of-three and retract closure of $W$ follow from the simplicial-set model axioms.

source.place: Theorem 4.7, generator families and adjunction argument, pp.1942-1943.

proof.text: For $K=\partial\Delta^n$ or $K=\Lambda_i^n$, $K$ is generated by its finitely many nondegenerate faces of $\Delta^n$. A map from $K$ to a filtered colimit is specified by images of these faces satisfying finitely many face relations; choose a common stage for those images and then a later common stage where the relations hold. Equality of two such maps is likewise equality on those finitely many faces and therefore holds at a common later stage. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,-)$ preserves filtered colimits, including $K=\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. By step 1 and the adjunction of step 2, $\operatorname{Hom}(F_sK,\operatorname{colim}_\beta A_\beta)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,\operatorname{colim}_\beta U_sA_\beta)=\operatorname{colim}_\beta\operatorname{Hom}(F_sK,A_\beta)$. Thus all generator domains satisfy the smallness hypothesis with the single regular cardinal $\aleph_0$, for arbitrary continuous chains of length $\omega$; no cardinal bound on $S$ is needed.

source.place: Theorem 4.7 proof, displayed four-line smallness calculation, p.1943; the finite-face factorization and equality arguments are expanded here.

proof.text: The families $I$ and $J$ are sets since $S$ is small. Completeness, cocompleteness and small Hom sets were established in step 1 and the common smallness cardinal in step 4. Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] to each family. This gives functorial weak factorization systems $(\mathrm{Cof},I^{\pitchfork})$ and $(L,J^{\pitchfork})$, where $\mathrm{Cof}={}^{\pitchfork}(I^{\pitchfork})$, $L={}^{\pitchfork}(J^{\pitchfork})$, and the left classes are the retracts of the corresponding relative cell maps. The right-class characterizations are those of step 3. It remains to prove $L=\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$; this does not follow just from the two factorizations.

source.place: Theorem 4.7 proof, condition (1) of Theorem 4.1 and small-object factorizations; condition (2) is verified by steps 6-8 instead of the invalid last sentence of the printed proof.

proof.text: Put $R(A)=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\circ A$. The finite-product comparisons, including the empty product, and the natural unit in [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] make $R(A)$ a strict $T$-algebra and $\eta_A:A\to R(A)$ an algebra map, naturally in $A$. Every sort of $R(A)$ is Kan and $\eta_A\in W$. For an algebra map $f:A\to B$, naturality gives $R(f)\eta_A=\eta_B f$. This uses no model structure on the algebra category.

source.place: Construction 3.3.6.1 and Propositions 3.3.6.4, 3.3.6.7, 3.3.6.9; applying the canonical product comparisons objectwise.

proof.text: For a sortwise Kan algebra $Z$, set $PZ(t)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\Delta^1\times\Delta^n,Z(t))$. Precomposition supplies simplicial operators, and postcomposition supplies the $T$-operations. Maps into a product are tuples of maps, so $PZ$ preserves the specified finite products. Let $c:Z\to PZ$ be constant paths and $e_0,e_1:PZ\to Z$ their endpoint maps. Transpose a lifting square for $(e_0,e_1)$ at any sort against a horn: it is the extension problem into $Z(t)$ from the pushout product of that horn with $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. This map is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], so $Z(t)$ being Kan gives the lift. Thus $(e_0,e_1):PZ\to Z\times Z$ lies in $\mathrm{Fib}$. For $e_a$, transpose against any boundary inclusion instead: its pushout product with $\{a\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is anodyne, since the endpoint inclusion is a dimension-one horn. Therefore each $e_a$ has the boundary lifting property and is a sortwise trivial fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Also $e_ac=1_Z$.

source.place: anodyneExtensions_pushoutObjObjι, lines 95-103, transposed explicitly to path endpoint lifting; Basic.lean:71-75 defines anodyne by lifting against Kan fibrations.

proof.text: Let $i:A\to B$ lie in $L$, so it lifts against every sortwise Kan fibration. Lifting the square with top $\eta_A:A\to RA$, bottom $B\to1$, and right $RA\to1$ gives $r:B\to RA$ with $ri=\eta_A$. The maps $\eta_B$ and $R(i)r$ from $B$ to $RB$ agree after $i$, since $R(i)ri=R(i)\eta_A=\eta_Bi$. Lift the square with left side $i$, top $c\eta_Bi:A\to P(RB)$, bottom $(\eta_B,R(i)r):B\to RB\times RB$, and right side $(e_0,e_1)$. It gives $H:B\to P(RB)$ with $e_0H=\eta_B$ and $e_1H=R(i)r$. As both endpoints are weak equivalences by step 7, two-out-of-three first shows $H\in W$ and then $R(i)r\in W$. Also $ri=\eta_A\in W$. Here is the needed elementary cancellation: on components, write $f=i_*$, $g=r_*$, $h=R(i)_*$. The bijections $gf$ and $hg$ make $g$ both surjective and injective, and then make $f$ bijective. For each sort and each basepoint $a$ of $|A(T_s)|$, apply exactly this algebra to the based group homomorphisms at $a,i(a),\eta_A(a),\eta_B(i(a))$; both composites are isomorphisms. Thus $i$ induces every required based group isomorphism and the component bijection, so $i\in W$. Empty sorts cause no exception: the component calculation still applies and there are then no based groups to test.

source.place: Repair of the acyclicity verification in Theorem 4.7, pp.1943-1944, using steps 6-7. Agent-written argument: lifting against the fibrant replacement and path endpoint fibration, followed by cancellation on components and based groups.

proof.text: Since $\mathrm{Fib}\cap W\subseteq\mathrm{Fib}$, lifting against all fibrations implies lifting against trivial fibrations, hence $L\subseteq\mathrm{Cof}$. Step 8 gives $L\subseteq W$. Conversely, for $f\in\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$, use the horn factorization of step 5 to write $f=pj$ with $j\in L$ and $p\in\mathrm{Fib}$. Step 8 and two-out-of-three give $p\in W$, so $p\in I^{\pitchfork}$. The lifting property of $f$ against $p$ gives a diagonal $d$ with $df=j$ and $pd=1$; the arrow maps $(1,d):f\to j$ and $(1,p):j\to f$ exhibit $f$ as a retract of $j$. The left lifting property is closed under retracts, so $f\in L$. Thus $L=\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$, and the two systems from step 5 are precisely the model weak factorization systems, with sortwise weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three and retract closure. Completeness and cocompleteness are from step 1. Finally, [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] identifies cofibrations with retracts of relative $I$-cell maps and supplies functoriality of both factorizations, proving all the assertions.

source.place: Conclusion of Theorem 4.7 via the now-verified acyclicity condition; explicit retract argument identifying trivial cofibrations.

lean.statement: theorem sorted_simplicial_algebra_model {S : Type u} (T : SortedTheory S) : HasLimitsOfSize.{u, u} (StrictSimplicialAlgebra T) ∧ HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (StrictSimplicialAlgebra T) ∧ ∃ (F : ∀ s : S, SSet.{u} ⥤ StrictSimplicialAlgebra T), (∀ s : S, Nonempty ((F s) ⊣ evaluation s)) ∧ ∃ (m : ModelCategory (StrictSimplicialAlgebra T)), m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = (fun _ _ f ↦ ∀ s : S, SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence ((evaluation s).map f)) ∧ m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations = (fun _ _ f ↦ ∀ s : S, SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.J.rlp ((evaluation s).map f)) ∧ m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations = (boundaryGenerators F).rlp.llp ∧ (boundaryGenerators F).rlp = (m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations ⊓ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences) ∧ (hornGenerators F).rlp = m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations ∧ HasFunctorialFactorization (transfiniteCompositions.{u} (coproducts.{u} (boundaryGenerators F)).pushouts) (boundaryGenerators F).rlp ∧ HasFunctorialFactorization (transfiniteCompositions.{u} (coproducts.{u} (hornGenerators F)).pushouts) (hornGenerators F).rlp ∧ (hornGenerators F).rlp.llp = (fun _ _ f ↦ (boundaryGenerators F).rlp.llp f ∧ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences f) ∧ (boundaryGenerators F).rlp.llp = (transfiniteCompositions.{u} (coproducts.{u} (boundaryGenerators F)).pushouts).retracts
